name: ablation_benchmark
description: NEEDS ONE PATH SUBSTITUTION BEFORE IT WILL RUN -- see _model_paths below. Does the DeepSets structure win GAMES, or only validation loss? The three flat-MLP ablation arms (REPRODUCE.md section 9) as the pure-network agent against SakkirinaSolo over the same 400 games each: the DeepSets control, the parameter-matched flat MLP, and the 22.57x-capacity flat MLP. All three were trained on one split with one seed through one loop, differing only in the network.
_why_games_and_not_just_val_loss: THE OFFLINE RANKING DOES NOT PREDICT PLAYING STRENGTH, so the ablation cannot
Re-scoring the six seed-benchmark checkpoints on the full validation split showed
the shipped model LAST of the six on every offline metric -- highest loss, lowest
accuracy, lowest AUC, highest Brier -- and FIRST on win rate at 80.25%. In the same
table seed 4 is best on accuracy and AUC and is the weakest player of the six at
69.25%. With six models and offline losses spanning 0.0154 that is not evidence of
anticorrelation, but it is a clear demonstration that the offline ranking is
uninformative about playing strength at these margins.
The ablation's offline result is much larger than those margins -- a 0.0293 loss gap
to the matched arm, about 2.7x the entire spread across the five DeepSets seeds,
at p < 1e-9 game-clustered. So it is not the same situation. But 'larger than the
case where offline failed to predict games' is an argument, not a measurement, and
_interchangeability_was_verified: BEFORE THIS CONFIG WAS WRITTEN, the three ONNX files were checked to be drop-in
loadable by Bots/src/DeepSetsCore.cs, which is not obvious: two of them are a
output   win_probability [batch_size, 1] float32, a RAW LOGIT
All three match that signature exactly, byte for byte the same as the shipped
model's. The flat models do their padding, flattening and concatenation INSIDE the
graph, so no new C# feature extractor is needed and DeepSetsCore.cs's
ValueNetworkEvaluator can load any of them unchanged.
The output scale was checked too, because a model that emitted a probability rather
than a logit would be silently sigmoided twice by the bot and would play like a
much flatter evaluator without erroring. On 400 real states the three span
pairwise correlated 0.88-0.93. Dynamic node counts from 1 to 128 all evaluate.
_check_before_interpreting: CHECK THE EVALUATIONS-PER-TURN COLUMN. THE FLAT ARMS SHOULD COME OUT LOWER.
python tools/aggregate_benchmark_results.py --config ablation_benchmark --out-dir $OUT_DIR
This is the opposite of the check seed_benchmark.json needs, and for a real reason:
there the three models were supposed to search equally and a low row meant a broken
export, whereas here the flat models genuinely ARE slower per inference and a low
row is the expected physics.
Measured on an x86 compute node, single-threaded, 5000 real validation states
(tools/compare_onnx_models.py): DeepSets 49.0 us median, matched 60.7 us (1.24x
slower), wide 240.0 us (4.7x slower).
EXPECTED RATIOS, relative to the deepsets row:
matched   0.81x to 0.94x
wide      0.20x to 0.48x
The two bounds are the two ends of a modelling assumption, not measurement error.
The LOW end assumes a turn's time is spent entirely on inference, so evaluations
scale as 1/inference_time. The HIGH end allows for the fixed per-evaluation search
cost -- move generation, tree bookkeeping, simulation -- which inference time adds
to rather than replaces. That fixed cost is about 127 us, solved from the only pair
of (inference us, evals/turn) points measured on the same hardware and config: the
invalid first seed run's ~700 us / ~1,430 evals against the shipped row's ~58 us /
6,401 evals (see seed_benchmark.json's _first_run_was_invalid).
So if the deepsets row lands near 6,400 evaluations per turn, expect roughly
5,200-6,000 for matched and 1,300-3,100 for wide.
A matched row ABOVE the deepsets row, or a wide row anywhere near it, means the
SOT_MODEL_PATH substitution did not take and the arm silently fell back to
GameRunner's own copy of the shipped model. The hash pin should catch that first,
but the pin is a set check and cannot tell one allowed model from another.
AND NOTE WHAT THIS DOES TO THE COMPARISON. The arms are NOT matched on search
volume; they are matched on wall clock, which is what a deployed agent actually
gets. A flat arm that loses is losing on the combination of evaluation quality and
evaluation rate, and this config cannot separate the two. That is the honest
framing of the result, and it is the right question for 'should we have built the
flat model instead' -- but it is the wrong question for 'is the set structure a
better evaluator'. Separating them needs SOT_TIME_SCALE on the faster side, the way
equal_effort.json does.
_model_paths: EVERY SOT_MODEL_PATH BELOW MUST BE EDITED BEFORE SUBMITTING. One substitution:
CHANGE_ME_HPCWORK -> the literal expansion of $HPCWORK on your cluster
(echo $HPCWORK on the login node), e.g. /hpcwork/yfl79180
THE PATHS MUST BE ABSOLUTE. Not a style preference -- a relative path is resolved
against two DIFFERENT working directories on the way to the bot:
- tools/benchmark_cluster.py checks os.path.isfile(SOT_MODEL_PATH) from wherever
the harness was invoked;
- the game runs with cwd=GameRunner/bin/Release/net8.0, and the bot calls
File.Exists on the same string from THERE.
So a relative path can satisfy the harness and still miss in the bot -- and a miss
in the bot is SILENT: DeepSetsBotExp logs the rejection and falls back to its normal
resolution, which finds GameRunner's own copy of the shipped model. All three arms
would then quietly benchmark the same model and return three statistically
indistinguishable rows.
$HPCWORK IS NOT EXPANDED. Nothing between this file and the bot runs a shell: the
env dict is passed verbatim into the child process, so a literal "$HPCWORK/..."
stays a literal dollar sign and the file is simply not found.
An unedited config cannot run by accident: tools/benchmark_cluster.py checks that
SOT_MODEL_PATH exists BEFORE launching the game and aborts the task with exit 1 and
no result file if it does not. CHANGE_ME_* paths fail that check.
_what_the_pin_does_and_does_not_guarante: allowed_onnx_sha256 lists all three hashes because the pin is checked per task
against whatever that task's SOT_MODEL_PATH names. That is a SET check, so it
guarantees 'this task loaded one of our three known models' -- it does NOT guarantee
'the matched row loaded the matched model'. The harness has one allowed list per
Here the three models differ enough that the evaluations-per-turn column will
expose a mix-up on its own, which is not true of seed_benchmark. Check it anyway:
and compare against REPRODUCE.md section 9. Every result JSON also records its
task's full env, so which path each matchup used is recoverable afterwards.
_comparability: seed_base 20260930 is new, so these are 400 games none of the other configs have
played. The three arms share it, so all three play the SAME 400 deals -- seed =
seed_base + task_id and task ids run contiguously across matchups, so arm N plays
seeds 20260930+400N.. which is a DIFFERENT 400 games per arm.
That is the same limitation seed_benchmark has and it is deliberate: reusing one
seed range across matchups would pair the arms but would also mean the harness
could not tell two arms' result files apart by task id. Read differences against
the Wilson intervals the aggregator prints, not as a ranking. Three arms at 400
games resolve about 6 points at 95% confidence; the offline gap predicts more than
that for wide and possibly less for matched.

matchups.label: deepsets
matchups.note: The control: the paper's architecture, retrained on the same split and seed as the two flat arms so the comparison is like-for-like. 73,089 parameters, val loss 0.4290, 78.65% accuracy, sha256 4619288b... Expect roughly 6,400 evaluations per turn, in line with the shipped row of seed_benchmark.

matchups.label: flat_matched
matchups.note: Parameter-matched flat MLP, 12691->5->128->64->1, 72,549 parameters (0.99x the control). Val loss 0.4635, 76.73% accuracy, sha256 bbbccfb7... 1.24x slower per inference on x86, so expect 0.81-0.94x the control's evaluations per turn. Note 61.9% of its weights are identically zero after the export flush -- matched by parameter COUNT, not by effective capacity; see REPRODUCE.md section 9.

matchups.label: flat_wide
matchups.note: Flat MLP with 22.57x the control's capacity, 12691->128->128->64->1, 1,649,409 parameters. Val loss 0.5325, 75.83% accuracy, sha256 26c396d8... This arm exists to foreclose the objection that the matched arm was starved: it is worse than matched offline on every metric and in every prestige bucket. 4.7x slower per inference, so expect only 0.20-0.48x the control's evaluations per turn -- it is doubly penalised here, and a heavy loss is the prediction rather than a surprise.
